title: Sleep scoring made easy—Semi-automated sleep analysis software and manual rescoring tools for basic sleep research in mice
author: Kreuzer, Polta, et al.

steps.title: Launch Sleep Scoring Software
steps.instruction: Open the LabVIEW 8.5 program; the graphical user interface appears. Choose one of the three executable modules: Manual Artifact Detection, Semi‑automated Sleep Scoring, or Rescoring.

steps.title: Prepare Animal Housing and Recording Schedule
steps.instruction: House the 14 mice in 26 cm × 26 cm cages with wood chips and nesting material inside noise‑reduced recording chambers. Maintain a 12 h light/12 h dark cycle (220 lx during the light period) at 24 °C ± 1 °C. Provide food and water ad libitum. Allow a 14‑day postoperative recovery and adaptation to the light/dark cycle. After recovery, record EEG/EMG for 23 h per day for at least three consecutive days, leaving a 1‑hour gap at the end of the dark period for animal maintenance if needed.

steps.title: Perform Surgical Implantation of Electrodes
steps.instruction: Anesthetize each mouse with isoflurane using a Univentor 410 unit (agnthós, Sweden) while positioned in an Angle Two Leica stereotactic frame (USA). Apply eye ointment, administer meloxicam 0.5 mg kg⁻¹ subcutaneously, and add meloxicam 0.5 mg kg⁻¹ to the drinking water for 8 days post‑surgery. Implant gold‑wire electrodes (≈100 µm ball‑tip) – two EEG, one ground, one differential, and two EMG – and solder them onto socket boards (Typ 861‑87‑008, preci‑dip, Switzerland). Connect the electrodes to a recording cable consisting of a 1× headstage amplifier (npi electronics, Germany), a SL‑10 slip‑ring commutator (Dragonfly, USA), and a custom‑balanced swivel with counterweight (Streicher, Austria).

steps.title: Set Up Recording Hardware and Parameters
steps.instruction: Connect the implanted electrodes to individual amplifiers (type DPA‑2FL, npi electronics, Germany). Set the amplification factor to 1000. Apply an analog band‑pass filter of 0.1–100 Hz to both EEG and EMG signals; additionally filter EMG online at 40–90 Hz. Digitize the signals at a sampling rate of 250 Hz using a Power 1401‑3 AD‑board and SPIKE2 system (Cambridge Electronic Design, UK). Store all recorded data for offline analysis.

steps.title: Prepare Data Files and Configure Scoring Parameters
steps.instruction: Export the EEG and EMG recordings as separate text‑file vectors. Launch the scoring routine via the GUI and select the desired module (Artifact Detection, Sleep Scoring, or Rescoring). Set the following parameters: sampling rate (Hz) matching acquisition (250 Hz), Butterworth filter order (as desired), high and low cutoff frequencies (0.5–31.75 Hz, adjustable), block length in seconds for RMS calculation, and a file tag to label the generated artifact, auto‑scoring, and rescoring vectors.

substeps.instruction: Enter file tag for output vectors.
